scenes.vo: Attackers aren't stopping at the network anymore. They're going after the controllers.
Are yours compromised? Could you prove they're not?
Without a golden baseline, a malicious change looks like routine engineering.

text.headline: A malicious change looks like *routine engineering.*

scenes.vo: And every vendor's software is different. Proprietary, priced in the thousands, and never built for security work.
Now imagine one tool for all of it.
This is PEAT. The Process Extraction and Analysis Tool, from Sandia National Laboratories.
Scan the network. Fingerprint every O-T device.

text.title: Fingerprint *every* OT device
text.sub: Discover hosts, then verify vendor and model.

scenes.vo: Pull the logic, configs, logs, and firmware. Ethernet or serial.

text.title: Pull the *evidence*
text.sub: Logic, configs, logs and firmware, straight off the device.

scenes.vo: Parse it all into one standard format.

text.title: One *standard format*
text.sub: Every vendor's data, normalized into one model.

scenes.vo: Diff against your golden config. Send results to Elastic or Splunk.

text.title: Spot the *change*
text.sub: Compare to your golden config, then send to your SIEM.

scenes.vo: Built with safety first. PEAT confirms what each device is before it collects anything, and pulls only what you ask for.

text.headline: Confirm first. *Collect carefully.*
items: Fingerprints one device at a time
Pulls only what you ask for

scenes.vo: PLCs. Protection relays. RTUs. And more, across over ten vendors.
PEAT itself runs on Linux, Windows, macOS, or Docker. Download it and run it, in minutes.
Want automation? Use PEAT as a Python library.

text.title: Automate it in *Python*
text.sub: Import PEAT and drive it from your own code.

scenes.vo: Need a new device? It's one self-contained Python module.

text.title: New device? *New module.*
text.sub: One self-contained Python class per device.

scenes.vo: And it costs nothing. Free and open source, GPL version three.
Know what your controllers are doing. Get PEAT on GitHub.
